title: Phenomenology of the experience of incongruence in the Cognition Congruence Tool (CCT): an exploratory mixed-methods study
summary: The study investigates how people experience inner congruence and incongruence in relation to a personal concern and whether questions asked during the process change this experience. Approximately 20 adults work on their concern together with a practitioner using the Cognition Congruence Tool. This tool is part of Process- and Embodiment-focused Psychology (PEP) and incorporates thoughts, feelings, and bodily experience. Participants verbalise predefined test statements, describe their sensations in brief interviews during the session, and subsequently supplement these descriptions with drawings on a body outline. Questionnaires are completed before and after the session. The aim is to better understand subjective experience, rather than to evaluate the effectiveness of the method.
conditions: Healthy volunteers; experience of congruence and incongruence (non-clinical personal concern)

interventions.name: A single session in which the Cognition-Congruence Tool (CCT) from Process and Embodiment-focused Psychology (PEP) is applied to a personal concern.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Capacity to provide informed consent and legal capacity
- Sufficient German language proficiency
- A genuine personal concern with an achievable desired outcome, with non-achievement experienced as aversive and achievement as appealing
- Written informed consent, including consent to audio recording of the participant
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute psychiatric disorder, particularly acute psychosis or acute suicidality
- Acute psychological crisis
- Severe personality disorder
- Unstable complex trauma-related disorder
- Acute substance intoxication
- Ongoing treatment with the practitioner conducting the session
